newsitem.title: USA: US natgas stocks seen flat to up 8 bcf in AGAs.
newsitem.headline: US natgas stocks seen flat to up 8 bcf in AGAs.

text.p: U.S. natural gas storage levels were expected to be unchanged to eight billion cubic feet (bcf) higher when weekly American Gas Association (AGA) data are released later today, industry sources said Wednesday.
The Reuter poll of industry players showed expectations ranged widely from a draw of 30 bcf to a build of 30 bcf for the week ended Nov 8. The four-week average build is 39 bcf.
"The first part of last week was cold, but later we were in the 60s (degrees F). I think we'll see a plus number," said one East Coast trader.
Last week's build was above expectations and closed the gap to last year to 233 bcf, or about eight percent.
Eastern stocks, at 96 percent of capacity last week, were roughly even with year-ago.

Despite the cold this week that should result in a significant draw in next week's report, traders said the stock deficit to 1995 should continue to narrow this month because of the record cold seen last November. Weekly drawdowns in November 1995 averaged 74 bcf.
In last report, producing region inventories at just 74 percent full continued to seriously lag 1995 levels at about 89 percent of capacity.

For the same week last year, total inventories fell 85 bcf, meaning a build today in the expected range would narrow the gap to 1995 to about 145 bcf. In 1995, eastern storage fell by 54 bcf, while producing stocks dropped by 18 bcf.
